verdict.tagline: Deep builds and classic action, despite rough UI edges.
for_you_if: you want deep character build variety
you enjoy complex isometric action role-playing games
not_for_you_if: you rely heavily on full controller support
you need clean high resolution UI scaling
you get frustrated by dead ends and backtracking

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players struggle with interface scaling and controller limitations.

claims.claim: The UI and interface become too small to view comfortably on 4K screens.

citations.review_text: Only 6 hours into the game and have played Diablo since it was launched in 90s. I feel bad now about having missed on Grim Dawn earlier. I agree the graphics are a bit outdated but the game design and game play are absolutely terrific. Still not sure it is meant for 4K screens as the interface becomes too tiny to view, but I guess you get used to things with time. Also wish I had a better way of tracking quests or knowing where to go, but I guess I have to learn more about the interface. Thoroughly enjoyable gameplay. Item Color tagging is different from Diablo which confuses me a bit but i love the game so far. I had this game for nearly 1.5 years before I am playing it seriously now. I wish I had begun the day I bought it.

Ancient but solid ARPG.  Tried a long time ago -- UI scaling was broken at 4K and controller support wasn't good, so I gave up.

At some point, they've mostly fixed both pain points.  Controller works as expected w/ Steam Input.  UI scaling is better at 4K as well.  A touch small for my taste but very playable.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that controller support is incomplete or poorly implemented, citing issues such as missing controller button prompts during tutorials, invisible mouse pointers in menus, and an inability to attack while moving.

citations.review_text: I bought this game years ago because it claimed to have full controller support. This is, at the very least, misleading. During the tutorial, the instructions only show keyboard controls, so you have no idea what buttons to press on the controller, in many cases there is no shortcut on controller but game doesn't tell you that. The menus are not at all optimised for controllers; they are clunky and unintuitive.

Game claims "full" Xbox controller support, by this is a lie.

First, during the early game tutorial, the instructions only show the keyboard controls, so you'll need to read the all of the controller settings yourself.

Second, the menus are not optimized to work with the controller at all. In menus, the right joystick acts as the mouse pointer, but its completely invisible. 

Skip this if you play primarily with controller.

it's a cool game i'm sure but not being able to attack while moving even with a controller tires me. So dont see this as me bashing the game but just warning fellow like minded people that you can't attack and move at the same time so each attack makes you stand still just aint fluid enough for me.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Progress reveals deep customization alongside endgame crashes and navigation friction.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the dual-class masteries and devotion systems as offering deep character customization and build variety.

citations.review_text: I was looking for a game similar to diablo with tons of dropped items and customization.  This game fit the bill exactly.  Dual class mechanic is brilliant.  Almost limitless upgrades to your character.

Great ARPG, perfected !

Positive
+ A lot of content and things to explore
+ Graphically excellent and runs on any hardware
+ Loot to collect, sort and hoard

Negative
- ?

There's an incredible depth of skills and synergies you can slam together to brake everything. Thats not mentioning the constilations and their addition to the builds. 

great game. play with mates or solo.

Insane levels of mechanical freedom.

Where do I even begin...

Some games are good for a few weeks. Some are great for a few months. Then there are games like Grim Dawn.

Games that refuse to die.

The older they get, the better they become. Every time you come back, it feels like you're experiencing them for the first time again. That's what real classics do. They don't chase trends,they become timeless.

That's Grim Dawn.

Whether you're playing alone or with friends, this game reminds me why I fell in love with ARPGs in the first place. It captures that feeling Titan Quest gave me, the darkness of Diablo, and the build freedom I always wanted from PoE1. Every fight makes you feel stronger. Every level matters. Every legendary drop makes you stop for a second and think, "Now we're talking."

The story is actually really good if you're into lore, but let's be honest... the gameplay is why we're all here.

And what gameplay it is.

The combat is satisfying. The loot is addictive. The Masteries are brilliant. The Devotion system is one of the best progression systems I've ever seen in an ARPG, and the amount of build variety is honestly ridiculous. Hundreds of hours later, you're still finding new combinations to try.

Then there's something that deserves even more praise.

No microtransactions.

No battle pass.

No seasonal FOMO.

No cash shop trying to squeeze every cent out of you.

Just an incredible game made by developers who clearly cared more about making something unforgettable than something endlessly monetized. You buy the game, you buy the expansions if you want more, and that's it. Imagine that.

If you're new, don't expect everything to click immediately. There is a learning curve. There are systems to understand. There are builds to experiment with. But that's exactly what makes the journey so rewarding. Every hour feels like progress, and every victory feels earned.

I've been smiling since I started playing again, and that's becoming rarer and rarer with modern games.

citations.review_text:
+: great skill's system, sweet loot, minion builds i love, offline and paying with friends, story, giant map with seamless huge locations.

-: inconvenient constellation system, barely visible obstacles so you running a lot of time into the "wall" (deadly in combat), loot filter is poor, craft system (forge) is inconvenient, locations is always the same even in never-ending rift, all map's random is removed block from one of roads and blocked other ways.

If you want better but same grind focused game - should give it a try!

would be a decent game if it wasn't for the labyrinth like map design, destroyed bridges, blocked off paths,  POI's disappearing from the map unless you're within a certain range, caves/underground passages often being the only means to progress further down the map, nothing is ever straight forward, makes revisiting certain areas even more annoying, traversing the map is just a massive pain in the ass and the longer you play the more annoying it gets, the game does some things well but honestly its so annoying to play i don't know if i'll start the new DLC...

[h1]This Game is NOT for Everyone[/h1]

The reason is simple:

[b]Even on Casual difficulty, this game is LONG.[/b]

I mean [b]VERY. VERY. LONG.[/b]

It took me around [b]29 hours[/b] to finish the base game, including some side missions and bounty missions.

And that's [b]WITHOUT the DLCs.[/b]

So I'm guessing there's probably a lot more hours waiting for me once I eventually get all the DLCs and start doing the other objectives and bounty missions.

[h1]THE CONFUSION[/h1]

I really love the game. It's cool, but it can get [b]VERY confusing[/b] when you're trying to figure out where you're supposed to go.

It's not like other RPGs where it's basically:

[quote]A → B → C → D → DONE[/quote]

Nope.

It's more like:

[quote]A → B → C → BACK TO A → GET ITEM → GO BACK TO B → GO TO D → RETURN TO C → ???[/quote]

You really need to take your time with this game.

And [b]READ.[/b]

I mean [b]READ EVERYTHING.[/b]

Read the dialogue, pay attention to encounters, and be careful about what you choose because [b]you can't always go back and change your decisions.[/b]

So don't just skip through everything and expect the game to tell you exactly what to do.

[h1]DON'T TRY TO SPEEDRUN THIS ♥♥♥♥[/h1]

This is definitely not a game where you should rush through the story just to finish it.

Take your time.

Explore.

Do side missions.

Read the dialogue.

Pay attention to what people are saying.

Otherwise you're probably going to end up wondering:

[quote][b]WHERE THE ♥♥♥♥ AM I SUPPOSED TO GO?[/b][/quote]

[h1]THE ENDING?[/h1]

I was expecting some kind of proper [b]cutscene or credits scene[/b] after finishing the game.

But...

[b]Nope.[/b]

Maybe there's something more with the DLCs, so I'll probably update this review once I eventually buy and play them.

[h1]AND THEN THERE'S THE PERFORMANCE[/h1]

I don't know WTF is wrong with this game, but every time I launch it my [b]PC fans go BRRRRRRRRRRRR.[/b]

Like th…

Definitely one of the best ARPGs I've played for a while.
I had problems with DX11, but when I switched to DX9 and limited my FPS to 144, 
everything worked like a charm—no more crashes and freezes. 
The story is very, very good, quests and exploring are mega good, and the talents and combinations that you can make are insane (I finished with 0 spells, all passives, making a dual-gun build that is so cool, hehe).
Bosses are solid. I'm a little tired of the game, so maybe I will come back next year to play the new DLC. Definitely worth the money (I got it for €13.84, base game and all DLCs, except the new one).
Definitely recommending it for ARPG fans; I think it was made in the old Titan Quest engine.

Tired of grinding the same campaign each season just to get to the "good stuff" (endgame)?
Grim Dawn rewards exploration, ground loot matters, and there are many side bosses and dungeons that are worth exploring.

Tired of rushing endgame to get economic advantage so you can fund your "real build"?

claims.claim: Reviewers report that class mastery choices cannot be reset for characters.

citations.review_text: Best ARPG I've ever played. Dual-class system and itemization creates endless possibilities for builds, yet doesn't feel overly complex to the point where you're overwhelmed and feel like you need a guide. You can go for whatever sounds cool to you and easily reallocate skill points on the fly - the only thing you're locked in to are your class choices for each character you make, but every class combination is viable. The lore and worldbuilding are also very compelling, and you can really dig deep into it via lore notes if you want to. Can't recommend Grim Dawn enough!

meaningless time sink
spend 100+ hours leveling character to 94, where you can actually play your build, then start leveling another character cause you can't reset masteries.
absolute trash design on top of outdated engine

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering sudden difficulty spikes and getting killed instantly by attacks on higher difficulties.

citations.review_text:
TLDR: A fun and deep game with a lots of effort put in it that doesn't respect your time, exemplifies pitfalls of the genre and is high off its farts. I like the game and will likely spend hundreds of hours on it but precisely because of that I will focus more on the negatives (i.e. I will now proceed to whine about everything I dislike about the game).

GENRE

This genre needs no introduction. If you know what Diablo/Sacred/Torchlight is you know what this is. I will write generally about the game and all of its DLCs as well (except Crucible because I don't have that one yet).

SETTING

What is somewhat unique is the victorian/western setting of your home faction and the aetherial enemy faction. Other elements like vaguely pagan/norse/egyptian aesthetic are less than new.

Sadly the story is mostly "everything went to ♥♥♥♥". Nothing wrong about that but since everything is miserable you get used to it. It loses its impact after you see X for Yth time. And you will. And the nature of the game means changes are limited. You can never really defeat the bad guys since they have to remain there to be farmed... That is what the genre is but it again blunts the impact of the story (at least for me).

CLASSES

There is a lot of classes and many combinations. On Normal difficulty, most things seem valid. Above that it does require some thinking and skill. Difficulty-wise game presents some occasional spikes in the form of certain enemies that just hit your weaker resistances and shred you (despite you without issues clearing the rest of that area). That can be very frustrating. After the latest DLC the balance is a bit... off? maybe

DIFFICULTIES

Like many other games in this genre you need to complete the game on normal with every character before you are allowed to start the (mostly) same game with the same character on higher difficulties. Now there are differences in enemy difficulty, loot drops, locations and such but I still strongly dislike this. I wish these game w…

I really love this game, in fact it's easily one of my favourite (if not THE favourite) ARPGs. The new mastery is fun and the overall quality of the content is high. Rich lore, tasteful music, amazing art.
But IMHO there are some weird balance decisions... 

The game currently almost feels like a "souls-like", which is also a genre I very much enjoy, but I believe it to be dissonant with what this game used to be. In fact since this game is built with an ancient engine, it feels wrong having to deal with all the twitchy dodge mechanics or you're dead.

Besides that, on higher difficulties like ultimate (and even worse on ascendant), you can die almost or even instantly to attacks and not processing even what happened, even with good defensive layers, high HP and overcapped res.

It's still an addictive game with overall high quality, but I still can't agree with the current balance. I want to recommend this, but the balance really leaves a sour taste...

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a completely free camera system.

citations.review_text: I've spent too many hours in this game probably. The mix of two classes plus a tree of bonuses makes every character unique in how it plays. It's an older game, but you forget that after about 5 minutes. It also has a completely free camera, no more getting stuck with one view of the world. I wish Diablo and POE had that. Makes such a difference.

Diablo 2 was a big part of my childhood, and I remember spending countless hours playing online with my friends. Grim Dawn is a spiritual successor to that game, fitting the tone and feel of Diablo 2 in a way that other diablo-likes never managed.

Made by the same team that worked on Titan Quest, you gain access to 2 masteries (1 at 2nd level, and another at 10th level) that give you a lot of customization in class-building. It's great for trial-and-error and building out interesting character builds. If skill tinkering is something you like, it'll scratch that itch.

In 2026, the new update brings a breath of fresh air to the game with revamped UI, combat animations and gameplay touches. The game might be a bit older, but the art style hits a good stylized spot that allows it to look great even today. The setting is an early industrialized fantasy, with pistols and rifles just as common as sword and sorcery.

The game feels good to play, gives a lot of customization options and lets you build your character out with unrestricted freedom. There is little to no hand-holding for the player, which might bring the bar for entry up a little, but if you like isometric hack-and-slash games, then stick with it, you won't be disappointed.
